title: Google Seeks to Raise $80 Billion for AI Infrastructure
summary: Google announced plans to raise $80 billion for AI infrastructure investment, including a $10 billion stock sale to Berkshire Hathaway as part of the plan. The move underscores the accelerating capital race among major technology companies to build AI computing capacity at scale. Google's aggressive spending posture is pressuring rivals to match its pace of investment.

title: Anthropic Makes Confidential IPO Filing
summary: Anthropic has confidentially filed preliminary paperwork for an initial public offering, according to multiple sources. The confidential filing allows the company to gauge investor interest before making financial disclosures public. The move marks a significant step toward a potential listing for one of the most closely watched AI startups.

title: Trump Signs AI Executive Order to Increase Government Oversight
summary: President Trump signed a new executive order directing AI companies to provide the federal government access to their most powerful models 30 days before public release. The order is a scaled-back version of a broader proposal Trump shelved last month. It represents the administration's latest attempt to establish federal oversight of frontier AI systems.

title: Alphabet's Mega Fundraising Shows the Value of Being a Public Company
summary: Alphabet's ability to tap equity markets for its AI infrastructure push has renewed the strategic value of being a publicly traded company, a dynamic largely absent from tech for the past 25 years. Private AI competitors must rely on venture capital and private debt at far greater cost. The analysis argues that the AI capital race is reshaping the competitive calculus between public incumbents and private challengers.

title: Why 'Nvidia Inside' Can Work in the PC Market
summary: As the world's only $5 trillion company, Nvidia has the brand power and ecosystem leverage to drive AI computing into consumer PCs in a way analogous to Intel's 'Intel Inside' campaign. The analysis argues that AI inference at the device level is a natural extension of Nvidia's data center dominance. The transition would further entrench Nvidia across the computing stack.

title: How AI Could Improve Economic Policymaking
summary: Artificial intelligence systems, with access to vast real-time data sets, could enable more-informed interest rate decisions and substantially better economic modeling for central banks and policymakers. Economists and technologists see AI as capable of identifying macro patterns that human analysts routinely miss. The piece explores how institutions like the Federal Reserve might integrate AI tools into their policy processes.

title: Turncoat AI Agents Emerge as the New Inside Hackers
summary: AI agents deployed inside corporate networks are emerging as a novel vector for insider cyber threats, security researchers warn. A due diligence firm was reportedly compromised via a malicious AI agent, illustrating how autonomous systems with broad internal access can be co-opted or manipulated. Experts are calling for new governance frameworks to constrain agent permissions and monitor for anomalous behavior.

title: Florida Sues OpenAI and Sam Altman Over Safety Concerns
summary: The state of Florida has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, making it one of the first states to bring legal action against an AI company and its leadership personally over safety practices. The suit reflects growing state-level regulatory activity targeting AI firms as federal policy remains unsettled. The legal challenge could influence how other states approach AI liability legislation.

title: OpenAI Taps Salesforce Executive to Lead Global Partnerships
summary: OpenAI has hired a senior executive from Salesforce to head its global partnerships function, signaling the company's accelerating push into enterprise sales and distribution. The hire brings experience scaling complex B2B relationships, a capability OpenAI needs as it competes for large corporate contracts. The appointment reflects OpenAI's broader shift toward commercial maturity.

title: SpaceX Targets $1.75 Trillion Valuation Ahead of IPO Roadshow
summary: SpaceX is seeking a valuation of $1.75 trillion as it prepares for an IPO roadshow, a figure that would rank it among the most valuable companies in the world at the time of listing. The target valuation reflects investor confidence in SpaceX's satellite internet and launch businesses. The roadshow will test whether public markets will support the premium Elon Musk's space company is seeking.

title: Enterprise Leaders Voice Concerns Over Rising AI Inference Costs
summary: Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy publicly raised concerns about the escalating cost of AI inference across his company's internal teams, joining a growing chorus of enterprise executives questioning AI ROI. His comments signal that the 'deploy first, optimize later' phase of enterprise AI adoption may be giving way to harder scrutiny of compute spend. The debate is likely to intensify as AI infrastructure costs compound.

title: Microsoft Launches Its First AI-Native Laptop
summary: Microsoft has introduced its first laptop designed from the ground up with AI capabilities integrated at both the hardware and software level, marking a departure from retrofitting AI features onto existing Windows devices. The device is built around dedicated AI processing hardware and optimized for on-device inference tasks. The launch positions Microsoft as a hardware player in the emerging AI PC category.

title: BYD Commits to Covering Financial Liability for Self-Driving Crashes
summary: Chinese automaker BYD has announced it will assume financial responsibility for accidents caused by its autonomous driving systems, a significant departure from industry norms where liability typically falls on drivers. The commitment is a competitive differentiator as Chinese EV makers aggressively roll out self-driving features. The move could pressure other autonomous vehicle companies to adopt similar liability frameworks.

title: SK Telecom Deploys Nvidia Digital Twins in Semiconductor Chip Fabs
summary: SK Telecom has deployed Nvidia's digital twin technology inside semiconductor manufacturing facilities, applying AI-powered simulation to complex industrial processes. The use case demonstrates how telecoms are expanding beyond connectivity into AI-enabled industrial operations. The partnership signals growing demand for digital twin capabilities in high-precision manufacturing environments.

title: Verizon Completes $1 Billion Spectrum Acquisition
summary: Verizon has completed a $1 billion spectrum purchase, strengthening its radio frequency holdings for 5G network expansion and future wireless capacity. The acquisition adds to Verizon's growing spectrum portfolio as the company competes with AT&T and T-Mobile for network leadership. Spectrum ownership remains a critical long-term asset in the wireless industry.

title: Canada's Private Equity Boom Is Leaving the Weakest Borrowers Exposed
summary: A surge in Canadian private equity activity is concentrating high-risk debt among the country's most financially vulnerable borrowers, raising concerns about credit quality in the PE-backed lending market. The share of borrowers rated as risky or highly leveraged has grown as PE deal flow accelerates. Analysts warn that a downturn could trigger cascading defaults among companies already operating near their debt limits.

title: Meta Plans ‘Hatch’ AI Agent Priced at Up to $200 a Month
summary: Meta is developing a consumer-facing AI agent called ‘Hatch’ that it is considering pricing at up to $200 per month, positioning the product in the premium AI assistant market alongside offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic. The move represents Meta’s ambition to monetize its AI investments directly through a high-priced subscription product aimed at power users. Details on specific features and a launch timeline have not yet been disclosed publicly.

title: SpaceX Sets $135 Per Share IPO Price, Plans to Raise $75 Billion
summary: SpaceX has set its IPO target price at $135 per share, planning to sell 555.6 million shares and raise approximately $75 billion—more than twice the size of any previous IPO. Shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX late next week. The offering uses a dual-class share structure giving CEO Elon Musk over 82% voting control after the listing.

title: Wall Street Expects SpaceX to Burn $350 Billion in Cash Through 2030
summary: Wall Street analysts project SpaceX will consume approximately $350 billion in cash through 2030, reflecting aggressive capital spending on Starship development, Starlink expansion, and other programs as the company prepares for its historic IPO. The scale of projected cash burn raises questions about capital needs even as SpaceX goes public. The projection underscores how demanding SpaceX’s growth ambitions are relative to its revenue trajectory.

title: Sam Altman-Backed Helion Triples Valuation to $15.5 Billion
summary: Nuclear fusion startup Helion has nearly tripled its valuation to $15.5 billion in a funding round led by Thrive Capital. The company, backed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, is working toward commercial fusion power and has attracted investor interest in part due to rising demand for clean energy to supply AI data centers. The round makes Helion one of the most valuable private energy companies in the world.

title: Snowflake CIO: Company Used Layoffs to Force Software Engineers to Adopt AI Tools
summary: Snowflake CIO Mike Blandina disclosed at the company’s annual customer conference in San Francisco that Snowflake deliberately used layoffs to compel its engineering team to adopt AI coding tools. Older, more senior engineers were the most resistant to the shift, and the workforce reduction created urgency for adoption. Snowflake is also managing AI costs by substituting cheaper models for certain tasks and uses its in-house AI coding agent CoCo, powered in part by Anthropic’s models.

title: Apple to Launch Revamped Siri in September Using Google Cloud and Nvidia Chips
summary: Apple is on track to release an overhauled Siri in September that will run partly on Google’s cloud servers powered by Nvidia’s Blackwell B200 chips. The company aims to process as much as possible on-device but will rely on external compute for more demanding inference. Apple is using Nvidia’s confidential computing feature to preserve its privacy standards while routing customer data through Google’s infrastructure.

title: Benchmark Raises $1.25 Billion Fund as Traditional VC Model Faces Strain
summary: Benchmark has raised a $1.25 billion fund as the firm adapts to growing pressure from a new wave of VC entrants and multibillion-dollar rival funds that have encroached on early-stage investing. The fundraise signals a strategic evolution for a firm historically known for small, concentrated bets in early-stage companies. The development reflects broader structural changes in the venture capital industry driven by the scale demands of AI-era companies.

title: Anthropic Urges Global Pause in AI Development, Warns of Self-Improvement Risk
summary: Anthropic, the $1 trillion AI startup, is calling on governments to coordinate a global pause in AI development and warning that frontier models are approaching the capability to improve themselves without human oversight. The company frames autonomous self-improvement as a critical risk threshold requiring international action before it is crossed. The call stands out because it comes from one of the leading commercial AI labs actively building the most capable models.

title: Phoenix Data-Center Boom Exposes the Problem of Who Pays for AI’s Power Costs
summary: Phoenix has emerged as a leading AI data center hub, and its largest utility is now seeking a 45% electricity-rate increase for data centers alongside a 14.5% increase for residential customers. The rate proposal has satisfied neither data center operators nor households and has exposed the structural difficulty of allocating AI’s infrastructure costs through existing utility frameworks. The Phoenix case may set a precedent for how other fast-growing data center markets handle the same conflict.

title: Meta Continues to Delay Release of New AI Model to External Developers
summary: Meta has repeatedly pushed back the timeline for releasing its latest frontier AI model to third-party developers, hampering its strategy to build an open-source developer ecosystem and monetize its large AI infrastructure investments. The ongoing delays put Meta at a disadvantage relative to OpenAI and Anthropic, which have been actively courting developers with their own models. No revised release date has been given.

title: SoftBank CEO Pledges $52 Billion for French AI Data Centers
summary: Masayoshi Son announced SoftBank will invest at least $52 billion in French AI data centers as part of an AI spending spree that has restored his standing after years of high-profile investment failures. The pledge is part of a broader global data center expansion strategy that SoftBank is pursuing across multiple countries. The announcement reinforces Son’s positioning of SoftBank as a major AI infrastructure investor rather than just a technology holding company.

title: Lawmakers Push to Ban AI-Enabled Personalized ‘Surveillance Pricing’
summary: U.S. legislators are working to ban the practice of using AI and personal data to charge individual consumers different prices for the same products, a technique critics call ‘surveillance pricing.’ The proposed legislation would restrict retailers and platforms from incorporating purchasing history, location, and browsing behavior into pricing algorithms. The push reflects growing regulatory concern about AI-driven tools being used to extract maximum prices from consumers without their knowledge.

title: CrowdStrike Reports First-Quarter Profit and Raises Full-Year Guidance
summary: CrowdStrike swung to profitability in its first quarter and raised its full-year financial outlook, marking a significant recovery milestone following the 2024 global IT outage it triggered. The results reflect restored customer demand for its cybersecurity platform and the company’s ability to retain and grow its client base despite reputational damage. The improved guidance signals management’s confidence in sustained growth through the remainder of the fiscal year.

title: Exclusive: Canada’s New AI Strategy Includes $500M Fund to Back Key Firms
summary: Canada’s federal government is set to unveil a national AI strategy that includes a $500 million fund to provide targeted support to key domestic AI companies and research institutions. The fund is designed to help Canadian AI firms compete against well-capitalized American and global rivals. The strategy represents the government’s most significant financial commitment to maintaining Canada’s position in the global AI race.

title: Canada’s New AI Strategy Sets Lofty Goals for Adoption and Economic Growth
summary: A special report on Canada’s newly released national AI strategy outlines ambitious targets for AI adoption across industries, framing the technology as central to Canada’s long-term productivity and competitiveness agenda. The strategy envisions broad AI deployment in both public and private sectors with goals linked to job creation and GDP growth. Observers note that while the ambitions are substantial, the plan is light on concrete implementation mechanisms and enforcement timelines.

title: Critics Warn Canada’s AI Strategy Lacks Meaningful Harm Safeguards
summary: Civil society organizations and critics are warning that Canada’s new AI strategy includes few concrete measures to prevent harms from AI systems such as bias, job displacement, and misinformation. The strategy’s emphasis on growth and adoption over safety and accountability has drawn criticism from groups calling for enforceable guardrails before broad deployment. The federal government has not addressed specific concerns about the absence of liability frameworks or independent oversight mechanisms.

title: EU Targets AI and Semiconductors in Intensified Digital Sovereignty Drive
summary: The European Union is stepping up its digital sovereignty agenda by targeting AI capabilities and semiconductor supply chains as strategic priorities requiring domestic investment and new regulatory measures. The push reflects European concern about over-dependence on U.S. and Asian technology providers for critical computing infrastructure. EU officials are preparing new initiatives to support domestic chip manufacturing and reduce exposure to third-party AI cloud services for sensitive government and enterprise applications.
